```{r}
#| include: false
has_tidy <- requireNamespace("tidyclust", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("generics", quietly = TRUE)
has_ggplot <- has_tidy && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_tidy, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                      dev.args = list(bg = "transparent"))
```

emeans works with tidymodels through two optional packages,
[tidyclust](https://tidyclust.tidymodels.org/) and
[generics](https://generics.r-lib.org/), and the code below runs only when
both are installed.

## broom-style methods

The broom-style verbs `tidy()`, `glance()` and `augment()` return plain data
frames, so no tibble is required to enjoy them.

```{r}
library(emeans)
library(generics)

set.seed(1)
df <- as.data.frame(rbind(
  matrix(rnorm(400, sd = 0.5), ncol = 2),
  matrix(rnorm(400, mean = 3, sd = 0.5), ncol = 2)
))
names(df) <- c("a", "b")

em_fit <- emeans(df, 2, threads = 2)
tidy(em_fit)
glance(em_fit)
head(augment(em_fit, df))
```

`augment()` reuses the training labels when `data` is the training set,
while passing `newdata` labels fresh observations through `predict()`
instead.

## The tidyclust engine

Loading tidyclust registers an `"emeans"` engine for `k_means()`, so the
usual specification needs nothing more than a different `set_engine()`:

```{r}
library(tidyclust)

spec <- k_means(num_clusters = 2) |>
  set_engine("emeans", nepochs = 3, threads = 2)
spec_fit <- fit(spec, ~ a + b, data = df)
spec_fit
```

Engine arguments such as `nepochs`, `spherical` and `threads` pass straight
through to `emeans()`, and the usual tidyclust helpers work on the result:

```{r}
extract_centroids(spec_fit)
head(extract_cluster_assignment(spec_fit), 3)
predict(spec_fit, df[1:5, ])
sse_within_total(spec_fit)
```

The within-cluster and total sums of squares that tidyclust expects come
straight from the fit, since `emeans()` adds them up in the same sweep that
labels the rows.

## Plotting with ggplot2

The tidyclust helpers return data frames, which ggplot2 happily takes as
they are; this chunk runs only when ggplot2 is installed as well.

```{r}
#| eval: !expr has_ggplot
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of 400 points in two groups, coloured green and blue by tidyclust cluster, with a large ringed dot at each cluster's centroid."
library(ggplot2)

points <- cbind(df, extract_cluster_assignment(spec_fit))
centers <- extract_centroids(spec_fit)
ink <- "#7C7799"

ggplot(points, aes(a, b, colour = .cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.4) +
  geom_point(data = centers, aes(fill = .cluster), shape = 21, size = 5,
             colour = "white", stroke = 1.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#1F9E80", "#5F6FE0"),
                      aesthetics = c("colour", "fill")) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
        text = element_text(colour = ink),
        axis.text = element_text(colour = ink),
        panel.grid = element_line(colour = adjustcolor(ink, alpha.f = 0.25)))
```
